text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We need a high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that jumps straight to the main content, making it easy for screen readers and keyboard users to bypass navigation. This is a non-negotiable feature because it greatly improves usability for users with disabilities. By accepting the trade-off of increased page load time due to the extra HTML element, we ensure that all users can access the main content quickly. This decision prioritizes accessibility over minor performance optimizations, which is essential for making EXCAVA usable by everyone.

name: Reader
text: A late-loading skip link traps keyboard users mid-tab before JavaScript runs, breaking the flow. A server-rendered skip link that hides until JavaScript confirms it works avoids this, but risks locking us into a rigid design if we later need to change the target. Test both with Playwright MCP: measure tab order and time-to-interactive across devices; if the server version adds >100ms delay or fails on slow networks, we keep the late-loading link and fix the timing.
